title: What If You Were The Only Man On An Island of 100 Native American Girls?
description:
What if you were the only man on an island of 100 Native American women? 🏝️

You wake up on a mysterious tropical beach after your boat sinks during a violent storm. Before you can figure out where you are, dozens of warriors emerge from the jungle, pointing their spears directly at you. They take you to a hidden village where you’re told something unbelievable: you have exactly 30 days to earn the trust of 100 women. If every warrior raises her spear, you can stay. But if even one refuses, you must leave.

In this animated what-if scenario, we imagine surviving on a remote island inhabited by a fictional Indigenous community with its own traditions, challenges, and secrets. From failing your first spear-throwing challenge to learning how to hunt, swim, and survive in the jungle, earning the villagers’ trust turns out to be much harder than expected.

At first, everyone sees you as a helpless outsider. But as the days pass, you begin helping the village, building useful inventions, and forming unexpected friendships. Your first vote might seem impossible to earn, but reaching all 100 would be an entirely different challenge.

Things become even more complicated when you discover mysterious writing left behind by a previous survivor, a secret emergency beacon, and a rescue ship approaching the island. What happened to the last man who washed ashore? Why does the village leader refuse to trust outsiders? And what happens when you’re forced to choose between returning home and protecting the people who saved you?

This 30-day survival adventure explores friendship, trust, mysterious island traditions, unexpected discoveries, and the difficult choices that come with being the only outsider in a hidden community. Could you earn all 100 spears before time runs out?

title: What If You and Your Crush Were the Last Two Humans Alive?
description:
What if Earth suddenly exploded, and the only person you managed to escape with was your crush? 🌍🚀 Imagine working at a rocket station when every alarm suddenly starts going off. You have just ten minutes before Earth is destroyed. You rush into the last available spaceship, but just as you’re about to launch, someone comes running toward you. It’s the girl you’ve secretly liked for years! Seconds later, you’re flying through space together, watching your entire planet disappear.In this animated what-if scenario, we imagine what would happen if you and your crush became the last two humans alive. With limited food, almost no fuel, and nowhere to call home, your only hope is a mysterious alien planet three days away. But what happens when you land on a beautiful new world filled with glowing forests, purple mountains, strange creatures, and two enormous moons?At first, surviving together seems impossible. You have to find food, build shelter, explore dangerous environments, and somehow avoid embarrassing yourself in front of your crush. But as the days pass, something unexpected happens. Between hilarious accidents, romantic evenings, and adopting an adorable alien creature named Biscuit, you slowly begin falling in love. 💕But this planet is hiding something incredible. Mysterious footprints appear near your camp, dangerous storms threaten your survival, and an ancient alien spaceship reveals a secret that could change humanity’s future forever. Could other humans have survived Earth’s destruction? And what happens when you discover that your new home might not be as empty as you thought?Over 30 unforgettable days, you and your crush must work together to survive, uncover the planet’s mysteries, and decide whether to leave your new world behind. title: What IF You Could See Everyone's Soulmate ?
description:
You walk into the kitchen on Saturday morning, and there's a name floating above your mom's head. Glowing gold letters: "Daniel." Your dad's name. Cute. Then your dad lowers his newspaper, and above his head there's a different name. "Claire." Everyone has one: the first name of the person they'd be happiest with for the rest of their life. You can see them all. Everyone's soulmate. Except your own.

In this story, you'll find out where the idea of an "other half" comes from, why the odds of finding one random soulmate would be about one in ten thousand, why most people marry someone who lived just a few blocks away, what love actually does to your brain, why couples' hearts can beat in sync, how 36 questions can make two strangers feel close, and how good we really are at spotting a lie.

Would YOU want to see the name above your own head? 👇

Every power has a price.

0:00 The Names
0:48 The Rules
1:40 The Love Doctor
2:43 The Wrong Names
3:26 Monday Morning
4:14 Claire
5:32 The Dance
6:47 A Red Thread
7:57 One Whisper
9:34 Ten Years
10:38 The Bench
12:20 New Rules
13:03 Saturday Morning

Science in this video:
- Plato's Symposium (about 2,400 years ago): Aristophanes' myth of humans split in half, the origin of the "other half"
- The red thread of fate: an East Asian legend of two people destined to meet
- With one random soulmate each, only about 1 in 10,000 people would ever find theirs (Randall Munroe, What If?, 2012)
- Bossard (1932): in 5,000 Philadelphia marriage licenses, a third of couples lived within five blocks of each other
- The spotlight effect: people think twice as many others notice them as actually do (Gilovich, Medvec & Savitsky, 2000)
- Intense romantic love activates the brain's reward system (Fisher, Aron & Brown, 2005)
- Couples sitting together tend to synchronize their heart rates and breathing (Ferrer & Helm, UC Davis, 2013)
- The mere-exposure effect: we tend to like what we see more often (Zajonc, 1968)
- The 36 questions that can create closeness between strangers (Aron et al., 1997)
- Couples who stayed together answered each other's "bids" for attention far more often (Gottman)
- The prefrontal cortex keeps maturing until about the mid-twenties
- People tell about 1–2 lies a day, and we spot lies only about 54% of the time (DePaulo et al., 1996; Bond & DePaulo, 2006)
- "Butterflies": adrenaline diverts blood away from the stomach
- Social rejection activates some of the same brain regions as physical pain (Eisenberger et al., 2003)
- Asking more follow-up questions makes people like you more (Huang et al., Harvard, 2017)
- Stable couples have about 5 positive interactions for every negative one during conflict (Gottman)

title: What IF College Assigned Your Crush as YOUR WIFE
description:
Your college just sent you a notification. Assigned spouse: Crush. Relationship: WIFE. 💍

BRO. THAT'S LITERALLY MY CRUSH.

Welcome to the Campus Partner Project, where students are assigned a fake husband or wife for 30 days. You have to share an apartment, manage a budget, complete relationship challenges, and survive weekly compatibility tests.

Starting compatibility: 50%.

One problem: I'm already in love with her. And somehow, between burning breakfast, getting jealous of another guy, and completely misunderstanding her, our compatibility drops to 39%. 💀

Now I have 30 days to figure out whether she actually likes me or if I'm just embarrassing myself.

question for the comments:

Day 30. The college gives you two options: YES or NO. Would you continue dating your assigned partner or walk away?

Subscribe before my compatibility score reaches 0%. My Crush is Watching.

Real fact in this episode: A famous 1950 MIT housing study found that people living closer together were more likely to become friends. Sometimes, simply spending time together can change everything.

title: What If We Had Never Invented Clothes? The Naked Truth of Evolution
description:
What If We Had Never Invented Clothes?
Imagine a world where no one ever put on a single garment. What would our civilization look like? Could humans have spread across the planet, survived the Ice Age, and built cities? In this video, we break down how clothing shaped evolution, health, culture, and the entire history of humanity.
In this video:
0:00 Intro: a world without clothes
1:10 When and why the first clothing appeared
3:00 How humans would have survived without it: climate and migration
5:15 Health: parasites, injuries, disease
7:20 How society and culture would change
9:30 Fashion, status, and identity: what we would lose
11:00 Final thoughts: could we have done without clothes?
Fascinating facts from the video:
🔹 Scientists estimate the age of clothing by studying the evolution of body lice: roughly 100,000 to 170,000 years
🔹 Without clothes, humans likely couldn't have settled the colder regions of Earth
🔹 Clothing influenced not only survival but also social norms and the concept of modesty
